prompt.en: You send QRL? and hear no direct reply. During the pause, a faint ongoing contact becomes audible. What should guide the next step?

text.en: Treat only a reply addressed to you as evidence that the channel is busy.

feedback.en: A contact can already be using the channel without answering your check. Listening supplies evidence too.

text.en: Repeat QRL? at higher power to establish which station has priority.

feedback.en: A busy check does not establish priority. Repeating over the contact would cover the traffic you just found.

text.en: Treat the heard contact as evidence of use and look for a clear channel.

feedback.en: The ongoing contact shows use even without a direct reply. Listen on a different clear frequency before calling.

text.en: Begin CQ during a fading dip because the contact is below a steady copy level.

feedback.en: A fading dip is not a free channel. The other stations may still be exchanging information.

explanation.en: An occupied channel can be heard without a reply addressed to you. Listening is part of the busy check.

prompt.en: A transmitter rises from 7 W to 28 W while the path stays steady. Assume a meter calibrated at 6 dB per S-unit. What change should you expect?

feedback.en: 28 / 7 = 4. Two power doublings give about 6 dB, or one calibrated S-unit upward.
This counts each power doubling as a full S-unit. Under the stated calibration, each doubling is about half an S-unit.
The power increased. A one-unit fall would correspond to quartering power under the same assumptions.
Half an S-unit is about 3 dB, or a doubling. This change includes two doublings.

explanation.en: The fourfold rise is two power doublings, about 6 dB. Under the stated calibration, that is one S-unit upward.

prompt.en: You turn a directional antenna and the strength meter drops. The distant station says its power is unchanged. Which conclusion is supported?

text.en: The drop measures a transmitter-power reduction despite the unchanged-power report.

feedback.en: The power-only shortcut requires an unchanged antenna. Turning it breaks that condition.

text.en: The drop shows poorer readability by the same number of report steps.

feedback.en: Strength and readability are different observations. A weaker signal can remain fully readable.

text.en: The drop proves the receiver gain setting changed during the turn.

feedback.en: The antenna changed, but the evidence does not show a receiver gain adjustment. Several causes can move the meter.

text.en: The drop may come from antenna direction, so it cannot isolate a transmitter-power change.

feedback.en: The antenna can change received strength at fixed transmitter power. Keep other conditions steady before using the power shortcut.

explanation.en: The calibrated power shortcut requires unchanged antennas, path, and receiver settings. An antenna turn breaks that comparison.
